top3.why: PhilaMOCA opens Halloween week with HAUNTEDWEEN, a little-seen 1991 slasher — exactly the kind of VHS-era curio this venue specializes in exhuming. Two back-to-back showtimes (7:00 and 7:30), so get there early for a seat. $10 at the door, in Callowhill, about a half-mile from the Broad Street Line's Spring Garden stop.

People's Headquarters runs a political-education session covering both "8 Can't Wait" and "8 to Abolition," then turns the conversation toward what abolition actually means for a local organizing program rather than the slogan. Free and discussion-based, open to newcomers — the listing doesn't give a street address, so confirm the exact location through the Action Network RSVP link.

DFA Records' noise-pop chameleons Guerilla Toss bring their frantic, genre-splicing live show to Ruba Club, a venue that always seems to book exactly this kind of weird. $23.79, 21+, doors at 7. In Northern Liberties, roughly a half-mile from the Market-Frankford Line's Spring Garden stop or the 57 bus up 2nd Street.

annotations.note: A free public reading of a new play exploring democracy, history and citizenship on the eve of the midterm election, presented with Theatre Exile; features THE BETSY ROSS BOOK OF THE DEAD and huntin / issa social thing, followed by audience discussion.
Flooding's slow-core, noise-rock, post-hardcore and post-punk blend, fronted by Rose Brown, at Johnny Brenda's.
Documentary-and-discussion series on how Philadelphia's past shapes the American story; this installment is "Renewal," free at the Ethical Society in Rittenhouse.
International Solidarity Committee's monthly solidarity-cinema night screens the Iranian road film 'Hit the Road'; suggested donation $6–12 at Nikki Lopez.
Philly DSA's ongoing virtual read-through of Ursula K. Le Guin's anarchist-utopia novel The Dispossessed, theory-light and open to newcomers.
PHL Code Club and Indy Hall's open-source Hacktoberfest meetup — submit pull requests to open-source projects through October for a shot at a prize.
Philadelphia Area Horror Meetup Group's casual watch-and-chat, held online — a 2025 short about a sculptor who falls for a talking hole in the wall.
A ballroom-scene vogue commentating class at The Rotunda, distinct from its regular Tuesday Vogue Practice Session.
Guided tour of the Art Museum's European galleries, featuring Monet, Pissarro, van Gogh and Cézanne.
Guided tour of the Rodin Museum's collection of Auguste Rodin's work; pay what you wish.
PFT's recurring virtual phone-bank, running most days this week, reaching out to elect pro-union, pro-public-education candidates across Bucks, Montgomery and Delaware counties.

top3.why: A documentary about two unhoused men turned community organizers in West Oakland's Wood Street encampment — at its peak the largest in Northern California — screens at Wooden Shoe as part of its regular film night. Free, pay-what-you-can in spirit; a sharp pairing of politics and film at exactly the bookstore built for it.

Lilyisthatyou brings her dreamy, confessional alt-pop to First Unitarian with support from James the Seventh — all-ages, R5 Productions' usual home for exactly this kind of show. Doors 7:30, show at 8.

A rally pressing the city to commit funds before Neighborhood Restorations/Prime Property sells off 925 affordable rental units across West and Southwest Philadelphia — a sale that could displace thousands of tenants and ripple through rents citywide. Free, held in front of a group of the company's own townhomes; the listing doesn't pin the exact block, so check the RSVP link for the meeting spot.

annotations.note: Woodmere's Halloween Film Frights series presents ¿Quién Puede Matar A Un Niño?, a celebrated 1976 Spanish horror film about an English couple finding a remote island's children turned sinister; in Spanish and English with English subtitles.
Smidley and Alltheflowers at Ruba Club, 21+, doors at 7.
Weekly listening-session series pairing an early live set with a classic-LP spin; October's resident is Taylor Kelly, a Philadelphia jazz/soul/funk vocalist with hip-hop and electronic touches.
LA art-rock trio Velvet Penny headlines a sliding-scale bill with World Assembly Body Opera and Keepsake at the Museum for Art in Wood.
Philly drag performers Pi & Onyx Ondyx host a viewing party for The Boulet Brothers' Dragula Season 7 at Strangelove's.
Wooden Shoe hosts a reading and generative poetry workshop with mk zariel, youth poet laureate of Madison — held online.
People's Music Supply's weekly curated-performance-plus-open-improvisation series at The Living Signal; this week's opener is a solo frictophone set.
An immersive close-up magic show at the Kimmel Center built around a fictional carnival owner's memorial, running most of this week.
UNITE HERE's volunteer canvass for pro-worker candidates in the Lehigh Valley, running daily most of this week; training provided for first-timers.
UNITE HERE's volunteer canvass for pro-worker candidates around East Stroudsburg, running daily most of this week; training provided for first-timers.

top3.why: Mannequin Pussy — Philly's own and one of the most acclaimed punk bands going — headline a benefit show for Carolyn, with Dark Thoughts, KulfiGirls, Commitment and Cult Objects rounding out the bill. All ages, $48.47, doors 6, show 6:30 — punk, benefit and all-ages in one package, the exact combination First Unitarian exists for.

The Dirty Girlz collective raises support for Amal, a postpartum mother of four in Gaza, with live music and poetry plus collage and bracelet-making stations at Wooden Shoe. A small, hands-on way to put solidarity into a room rather than just a post.

Lightbox Film Center resurfaces Seijun Suzuki's rare, irreverent Capone Cries A Lot — a 1920s naniwa-bushi singer mistakes Al Capone for the US president and tries to win him over, with a jazz band under the bridge playing hybrid blues-rōkyoku the whole way through. Exactly the kind of genuinely obscure repertory pick that justifies checking a film society's calendar instead of a chain theater's.

annotations.note: Seldom-seen weird-and-wonderful short films drawn from Philadelphia archives and museums, at PhilaMOCA.
Philadelphia's first-ever body-horror festival: burlesque acts inspired by body horror, movie trivia, a silent auction, vendors and lectures, in Manayunk.
Original indie horror short screenings, a filmmaker-and-horror-enthusiast mixer, and a costume contest at The Velvet Whip.
A live comic-book reading with local artists and a musical interlude from BORBS, plus a costume contest, in West Philly.
A drag-meets-Broadway variety show at Club 624, with Barrymore Award winner Danny Wilfred among this month's cast.
Korean group LEENALCHI, known for fusing traditional pansori with electronic production, at Asian Arts Initiative.
PHP x Philly's monthly meetup pitches silly ideas Shark-Tank style; this edition is Whimsy Tank.
Iffy Books' monthly Speculative Futures Reading Group discusses Katsuhiro Otomo's Akira, Volume 1.
Hands-on analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog transfer session for VHS tapes and audio cassettes at Iffy Books.
A low-key, bring-your-own-book reading social at Indy Hall's clubhouse, held the 2nd and 4th Wednesday of each month.
Poet-tree en Motion, a poetry-and-movement program at The Rotunda, distinct from its standing Wednesday jam session.
A guided tour of Wharton Esherick's handbuilt home and studio in Malvern, running most of this week.
Transylvanian Nipple Productions' long-running Rocky Horror Picture Show shadow-cast at City Winery, running several nights this week.

top3.why: The world premiere of Car Brain, a feature documentary on parking and Philly's car-ownership crisis, follows the PPA, bike activists, and Bok's own Simon Firth of Transport Cycles — directed by a former Bok Lead Ambassador. A hyperlocal film about a fight that's been playing out on Philadelphia's streets for years, debuting in the building some of its subjects work out of.

Fabrika turns Rocky Horror into a fully immersive live production for its third year running — drag, burlesque, aerial, and fire performers replacing the screen entirely rather than just shadow-casting over it. In Fishtown, a few blocks from the Market-Frankford Line's Berks stop.
Ars Nova Workshop brings rising South African saxophonist Linda Sikhakhane and his band to Solar Myth for a rare Philly date — 21+, on South Broad just a few blocks from home turf.

annotations.note: Power-pop rock icon Paul Collins, formerly of The Nerves and The Beat (his song "Hanging on the Telephone" became a hit for Blondie), at PhilaMOCA.
FAFIO ("f*** around and figure it out") is Iffy Books' no-instructor tech meetup for beginners, learning collaboratively via zines and trial and error.
SAZÓN: SOY EMO, an emo-Latin night at Underground Arts with Agent DMZ, WHOISTI?, and Kyree4Kyng.
Out-of-town death rock/goth/punk act Excess Blood (PDX) with Acid Test at Cousin Danny's.
Live improvised film scoring from Tom Spiker's Mobile Pleasure Lounge at Black Squirrel Club.
The Rosenbach's Behind the Bookcase series traces vampire fiction from Carmilla to Dracula — sold out, but worth the waitlist for next time.
El Conejo en el Faro Film Club's weekly Latin American cinema night at the Philadelphia Ethical Society, discussion in Spanish or English.
Miss Lisa Lisa's Drag Show, billed as Philadelphia's longest-running drag show, at Bob & Barbara's Lounge.
Van Cliburn gold medalist Yunchan Lim plays Rachmaninoff's Third Piano Concerto with the Philadelphia Orchestra, running several nights this week.

top3.why: Philly punk mainstays Thin Lips headline the tenth anniversary of this DIY house venue's Mischief Night tradition, with Superweaks opening. A decade of the same scrappy show at the same scrappy room is its own kind of occasion. In West Philly's Walnut Hill, near the 34/36 trolley on Baltimore Ave at 55th.

The Hamdeli Project and Penn's Middle East Center co-host a screening of An Eye for an Eye with a live Q&A from director Tanaz Eshaghian and producer/cinematographer Gelareh Kiazand, moderated by a Penn music-studies PhD candidate. Suggested donation $10–20; on South Broad in Center City.

Blush debut their new single live at PhilaMOCA with a stacked support bill — riot grrrl mayhem from Outcry, dreamy sounds from Her Side of the Bed, and high-energy Paratopia — plus a spooky artist market before the music starts. $17.20.

annotations.note: Emerging Haitian-American jazz vocalist Danielle Angrand, a YoungArts-recognized talent who has shared stages with Buster Williams and Emmet Cohen, at The Velvet Whip.
Vocalist Mi'cal Beckham honors Billie Holiday with interpretations of "God Bless the Child," "Good Morning Heartache," and "My Man" at Woodmere.
Roberta Faceplant, Philadelphia's own cowpunk outfit fronted by Katie Feeney, at Secondhand Ranch.
Philly DSA's Halloween costume party and fundraiser at Nikki Lopez, with a costume contest and raffle.
Violinist Sheng-Ching of Delirium Musicum performs entirely in the dark at the Philadelphia Ethical Society.
The stage mystery Clue runs several nights this week at Hershey Theatre.

top3.why: Ink & Dagger — the band whose horror-punk, screamo-adjacent chaos helped define '90s Philly hardcore — play Drexel's Creese Student Center in University City, co-presented by WKDU 91.7FM. $37.14, doors 8, show 9. A genuinely rare date for a band that doesn't play often.

A rare theatrical screening of Ken Russell's The Devils — the 1971 historical horror so controversial on release it was cut, banned, and effectively suppressed for decades, and still carries an NC-17. Four showtimes today (1:00, 4:00, 7:00, 9:30); this is the kind of film you don't get many more chances to see on a real screen.

Philly black-metal/horror-punk outfit Devil Master celebrate a decade together and a new record with Zorn, Coffin Dust, Diabolus, Satanic Magick, and Early Grave — moved last-minute from First Unitarian to this American Legion hall in Upper Darby. $25.81, doors 7:30, show 8. Outside city limits but reachable via the Market–Frankford Line to 69th Street Terminal, about a 20-minute ride from Center City.

annotations.note: Making Time's Pure Halloween bill at Franklin Music Hall stacks Boy Harsher, Model/Actriz, Conducta, a Marie Davidson DJ set, Kassie Krut, Dave P, and Klip Collective visuals.
Dancing Ferret Concerts' Dracula's Ball at Underground Arts headlined by EBM/industrial legends Lords of Acid, with Tapping the Vein.
A community town hall with State Rep. Andre D. Carroll on what can be done in Northwest Philadelphia, with food and kids' activities, in Germantown.
Dance Macabre, a goth after-hours Halloween dance party at Sanctuary in West Philly.
Let's Get Spoooooky Kiki Ball Part 2 at The Rotunda — ballroom-scene programming distinct from its standing weekly Vogue Practice Session.
The Darryl Yokley Quartet celebrates the music of Coltrane and Monk at Chris' Jazz Cafe.
A lecture, pizza lunch and painting session on the Guerrilla Girls, the anonymous feminist artist-activist collective, at CraftNation.
A Frankenstein pop-up exhibit at the Mütter Museum, included with admission, running on select dates through the month.

top3.why: Ben Gucciardi launches Arguments, his new collection from Persea Books, alongside fellow poets Fatemeh Shams and Grady Chambers — three distinctive voices on power, place, and memory, reading together at exactly the kind of bookstore that takes poetry about power seriously.

Lightbox Film Center screens Roy From Space, a lost-for-40-years Mexican animated sci-fi feature — only the third animated feature ever made in Mexico — newly restored from the original 35mm negative by Deaf Crocodile. Outsider animation loosely riffing on 1930s Flash Gordon serials; the rare-revival pick of the week.
heavens to betsy and Calamity Jane play First Unitarian — R5 Productions' usual all-ages home for exactly this kind of bill. $42.29, doors 7:30, show 8.

annotations.note: Bad Luck 13 Riot Extravaganza, a hardcore/metalpunk bill at Underground Arts featuring Chopped Up, Hard Turf, Sålik, Cheddabreed, and RingRust.
Vocalist Chelsea Reed and the Philly Pops Jazz Combo celebrate the classic jazz songbook of Philadelphia's own, at First Presbyterian Church.
Pianist Agustin Muriago blends folk rhythms from across the Americas with classical and jazz influences, at the Philadelphia Ethical Society.
A GOTV rally and door-knocking canvass in Lehigh County for Mark Pinsley, Bob Brooks and other down-ballot candidates, with guest speakers including Lehigh County Executive Joshua Siegel.
Atlanta's Silly Goose brings its "Set It Off" tour to Warehouse on Watts with Cheem and Muttlee.
